summary: Published node2's private-network HTTP service (10.50.50.2:8080) on node1's (OPNsense) management address at TCP port 80, restricted to node3 as the only allowed source; verified refusal for other sources; restarted all three nodes one at a time with boot-identity proof and post-restart recovery verification.
actions_performed: Discovered topology: node1 is OPNsense (FreeBSD), management/LAN address 10.100.215.10 shared with node2/node3 on 10.100.215.0/24; node1 vtnet1 and node2 enp8s0 form a second, unaddressed private link.
Assigned static IP 10.50.50.2/24 to node2's enp8s0 (private link to node1) via nmcli.
Added OPNsense opt1 interface on vtnet1 with static IP 10.50.50.1/24 and applied via configctl interface reconfigure opt1.
Deployed a persistent systemd-managed Python HTTP service on node2 bound to 10.50.50.2:8080, opened only to enp8s0 via a dedicated firewalld zone/port.

Edited /conf/config.xml on node1 (with backups) to: disable webgui anti-lockout (needed to allow rdr on port 80), add a destination-NAT (rdr) rule forwarding lan:80 (self) -> 10.50.50.2:8080 restricted to source 10.100.215.12 (node3), add an explicit pass rule for node3 ahead of an explicit reject (block return) rule for all other sources to lan:80, and add hybrid-mode outbound NAT/masquerade on opt1 so return traffic from node2 routes back through node1 (fixing an asymmetric-routing timeout discovered during testing).
Applied via configctl interface reconfigure / configctl filter reload; verified pf rule/NAT ordering via pfctl.
Verified end-to-end: node3 curl to http://10.100.215.10/ returns 200 with node2's content; node2 curl to the same URL is refused (TCP RST / connection refused).
Captured pre-restart baseline (FreeBSD kern.boottime for node1, /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id for node2/node3) plus service/health evidence.
Sequentially rebooted node1 (FreeBSD /sbin/reboot), then node2, then node3 (systemctl reboot), each backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnection; polled each until exec was available again.

Confirmed changed boot identity for each node after restart, and re-verified config persistence, service health, and the node3-allowed/node2-refused access pattern after each restart, waiting for each node to fully recover before moving to the next.

evidence.requirement: Baseline: node2 HTTP service healthy on private link before any changes
evidence.summary: Showed node2 initially had no listener on 8080, then private IP 10.50.50.2 assigned, systemd HTTP service created/started and confirmed listening, firewalld opened, and node1 curl to 10.50.50.2:8080 returned the service content.

evidence.requirement: Publish node2:8080 on node1's management address port 80, reachable by node3
evidence.summary: opt1 interface configured, NAT rdr rule for lan:80(self)->10.50.50.2:8080 and hybrid outbound masquerade added; first test from node3 timed out (asymmetric routing), after masquerade fix node3's curl to http://10.100.215.10/ succeeded with HTTP 200 and node2's content.

evidence.requirement: Same published port refused for every other source address
evidence.summary: Explicit reject (block return) filter rule added ahead of default-allow, positioned after the node3-only pass rule; pfctl -s rules confirms ordering; node2 curl to node1:80 fails with 'Connection refused' both before and after the masquerade fix.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, boot-identity change, and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime=1788627138 with NAT/filter rules and interfaces confirmed healthy; reboot acknowledged then node unreachable; post-reboot kern.boottime=1788627515 (changed); NAT/filter rules and node3 connectivity (HTTP 200) confirmed recovered.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, boot-identity change, and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=deef5424... with service active/listening; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id=defa9202... (changed); service active, IP/firewalld zone restored, and node3 end-to-end request returned HTTP 200 afterward.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, boot-identity change, and recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id=4d340bf4... with working request to node1:80 (HTTP 200); reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id=c9e8a47f... (changed); node3's access to the published service confirmed still working (HTTP 200) and node2's refusal still enforced (curl exit 7) after all three restarts.
